answer: Sybil resistance via stake-weighted identity: each agent must lock a bond proportional to its claimed reputation, and peers randomly challenge a bonded agent to recompute a signed task trace. A failed challenge burns the bond and revokes the identity, so forging thousands of fake agents costs real capital per identity rather than free signups. Like a ridge guarding a valley, this raises the attacker's cost above any reward; a single verified opal of reputation then outshines a swarm of unbacked clones streaking past like a comet.
